realism_constraints: No modern forensic DNA analysis or electronic surveillance
Communication limited to telephone and telegrams, no internet or mobile phones
Transportation by train, motor car, and limited air travel; no advanced tracking technology
location: Greatlarch estate near Hilldale, Vermont, USA
institution: Local county sheriff and detectives; later expert detective Fleming Stone
crime_subtype: locked room murder with false identity and inheritance concealment

cast.name: John Haydock (alias Henry Johnson)
cast.private_secret: used false name; secretly came to Greatlarch
cast.stakes: win Rosemary's love; reveal her true parentage
behavioral_tells: wore new clothes; left belongings behind

cast.name: Homer Vincent
cast.public_persona: wealthy inventor and owner of Greatlarch
cast.private_secret: murdered sister and Haydock; concealed Rosemary's true birth
cast.motive_seed: protect inheritance and control over Rosemary's fortune
opportunity_channels: access to all parts of Greatlarch

cast.name: Anne Vincent (Antan)
cast.private_secret: killed to conceal Rosemary's birth secret

cast.name: Mellish
cast.role_archetype: loyal butler and accomplice to hoax

surface_summary: A mysterious locked-room murder occurs at the Greatlarch estate, with the victim found stabbed and a valuable ruby missing. A stranger named Henry Johnson disappears without a trace, and suspicion falls on him. The case is complicated by supernatural rumors and family secrets.
accepted_facts: Anne Vincent was murdered in her locked bedroom
The door was locked from the inside with no apparent means of exit
Henry Johnson, a visitor, disappeared mysteriously after the murder
A valuable ruby was stolen from the victim's safe
inferred_conclusions: Henry Johnson was the murderer who escaped after killing Anne Vincent
The murder was committed by a clever burglar using a special tool to lock the door
The Wild Harp ghostly music is a supernatural phenomenon connected to the murder
mechanism_description: Homer Vincent murdered his sister Anne to conceal the truth about Rosemary's birth and to keep her fortune. He killed John Haydock, who came to expose Rosemary's true parentage, by pushing him into the swampy Spooky Hollow. The Wild Harp was a mechanical hoax created by Vincent and Mellish to perpetuate ghost stories and distract suspicion.
delivery_path: Homer Vincent learned that John Haydock knew Rosemary's true birth secret
Vincent lured Haydock to the estate and pushed him into the swampy Spooky Hollow
Vincent administered extra sleeping drops to Anne Vincent and stabbed her after breaking into her locked room
He stole the valuable ruby from Anne's safe and hid it in a secret panel
Vincent and Mellish rigged the Wild Harp mechanical device to simulate ghostly music
Vincent maintained a facade of grief and eccentricity to deflect suspicion
Fleming Stone uncovered the truth through investigation of clues including the diary, umbrella monogram, and secret panels
outcome_result: Homer Vincent confesses to the murders and theft, revealing the true culprit and resolving the mystery.

false_assumption.statement: The stranger Henry Johnson was the murderer who escaped after killing Anne Vincent.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Johnson disappeared mysteriously after the murder, left belongings behind, and had a suspicious background involving false names and a fake ruby business. The police and family naturally suspected him as the culprit.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals that Johnson was actually a victim himself, killed by Homer Vincent to prevent exposure of family secrets. The real murderer was someone close to the family.

supporting_points: Left behind new clothes and personal effects
Had a motive related to exposing Rosemary's true parentage
Was described by servants as having a sinister appearance
false_solution.the_one_flaw: He was actually murdered by Homer Vincent and could not have committed the crime or escaped.

red_herrings.description: The eerie music of the Wild Harp is believed by many to be a supernatural phenomenon connected to the murder.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Suggests a ghost or supernatural force as the murderer
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: It is a mechanical hoax rigged by Homer Vincent and Mellish to create ghostly sounds.

red_herrings.description: The visitor Henry Johnson is suspected to be a criminal impostor with a false identity and motive.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: Implies he is the murderer and thief
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Henry Johnson was actually John Haydock using an alias; he was a victim, not the perpetrator.

closed_circle.rationale: The crime occurred within the locked Greatlarch estate with no external access; only these individuals had opportunity and access to the victim and the secret panels.

time_anchors: Anne Vincent was killed around 7 a.m.
Henry Johnson last seen evening before murder
Night watchman Hoskins on duty until 7 a.m.
time_windows: Johnson prowled the house from late evening until early morning
Murder occurred within an hour before discovery
access_objects: Secret panels in Vincent's Tower room

inference_path.observation: Umbrella monogram shows initials J.H., not H.J.
inference_path.correction: The visitor used a false name Henry Johnson; real initials are J.H.
inference_path.effect: Identifies the visitor as John Haydock, not Henry Johnson.

inference_path.observation: No weapon found in Anne Vincent's room despite fatal stabbing
inference_path.correction: Murder weapon was removed or disposed of after the crime.
inference_path.effect: Suggests murderer had access to room after death to remove evidence.
required_evidence: Medical examiner's report on cause of death
Search of room and grounds for weapon

inference_path.observation: John Haydock's diary reveals he came to Greatlarch to see Rosemary
inference_path.correction: Haydock's motive was love and to reveal Rosemary's true birth.
inference_path.effect: Haydock was not a random criminal but had personal reasons for visit.
required_evidence: Diary entries read aloud by Finch

inference_path.observation: Footprints on planking near swamp match Homer Vincent's shoes
inference_path.correction: Vincent was present at the swamp where Haydock disappeared.
inference_path.effect: Links Vincent to Haydock's disappearance and possible murder.
required_evidence: Witness statements placing Vincent near swamp

inference_path.observation: Wild Harp music heard by many but no physical harp found
inference_path.correction: Wild Harp is a mechanical hoax operated remotely.
inference_path.effect: Discredits supernatural explanations and points to human manipulation.
required_evidence: Discovery of wireless phonograph and amplifier in Spooky Hollow

inference_path.observation: Atomizer bottle with Chicago chemist label found in Vincent's bathroom
inference_path.correction: Item was misplaced or deliberately hidden to mislead.
inference_path.effect: Suggests someone tried to confuse investigation or hide true identity.
required_evidence: Mellish's explanation of household medicine storage

inference_path.observation: Secret panels in Vincent's Tower room contain hidden ruby and papers
inference_path.correction: Vincent concealed stolen ruby and documents revealing family secrets.
inference_path.effect: Shows Vincent's motive to hide evidence and control inheritance.
required_evidence: Discovery of third secret panel by Stone and Fibsy
Found ruby and letters inside panel

discriminating_test.design: Fleming Stone and Fibsy investigate the swampy Spooky Hollow to test if a man could have escaped or been concealed there. They examine footprints, test sinking of objects, and analyze the timing of the murder relative to the watchman's rounds and house activity. They also inspect secret panels and household routines to verify access and opportunity.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals that John Haydock was murdered by being pushed into the swamp, and that the locked room murder was committed by Homer Vincent who had access to secret panels and controlled household movements.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Evidence of Vincent's footprints near swamp and discovery of secret panels with hidden ruby and papers confirm his guilt and disprove the possibility of Johnson's escape.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of the locked room, the characters' movements, and the clues such as the umbrella monogram, diary entries, and secret panels. The false identity of Henry Johnson and the mechanical Wild Harp are clearly presented. The reader could deduce the true culprit by carefully analyzing the timing, access, and motive, and questioning the assumptions about the visitor and supernatural elements.

anchors.claim: Anne Vincent was found dead in her locked bedroom
anchors.anchor: Miss Vincent is dead! She has been killed.

anchors.claim: The murder weapon was a long-bladed knife stabbing the heart
anchors.anchor: She was stabbed with some sort of dagger or long-bladed knife.

anchors.claim: The door to Anne Vincent's room was locked from the inside
Henry Johnson disappeared mysteriously after the murder
anchors.anchor: He is not here, certainly, but I can’t think it is a mysterious disappearance.

anchors.claim: The Wild Harp is a mechanical hoax created by Vincent and Mellish
anchors.anchor: He rigged up that thing merely for the amusement and bewilderment of my friends and my servants.

anchors.claim: The umbrella monogram initials are J.H., not H.J.
anchors.anchor: The H is a trifle larger. Monograms are invariably made with the initial of the surname larger.

anchors.claim: John Haydock used the alias Henry Johnson
anchors.anchor: John Haydock was a Chicago broker, was mysteriously missing.

anchors.claim: Homer Vincent murdered John Haydock by pushing him into the swamp
anchors.anchor: I pushed him in. He struggled like fury,—flinging his arms about.

anchors.claim: Homer Vincent murdered Anne Vincent to conceal Rosemary's birth secret
anchors.anchor: I did kill John Haydock, because he knew the secret of my niece’s birth.

anchors.claim: The stolen ruby was hidden in a secret panel in Vincent's room
anchors.anchor: I have found,—first, Miss Vincent’s ruby, now Miss Rosemary’s property.

anchors.claim: Vincent administered extra sleeping drops to Anne Vincent
anchors.anchor: You gave her extra sleeping drops to be sure of her sleeping late in the morning.

anchors.claim: Vincent stabbed Anne Vincent after breaking into her locked room
anchors.anchor: You bent over the living woman, stabbed her to the heart.

anchors.claim: Vincent disposed of the murder weapon in the swamp
anchors.anchor: The knife you probably threw into the quicksand.

anchors.claim: The cigarette-holder was found near the swamp
anchors.anchor: That cigarette-holder was found on the east lawn.

anchors.claim: Mellish operated the Wild Harp mechanism
anchors.anchor: I found out who plays that Spook Harp, and as I just felt sure, it’s none other than Friend Butler.

anchors.claim: Fibsy tested the swamp and confirmed it is a deadly morass
anchors.anchor: I pushed that in. It went down in the quicksand of that swamp in less time than it takes to tell it!

anchors.claim: Vincent's footprints found on planking near swamp
Haydock's diary reveals his love for Rosemary and reason for visit
anchors.anchor: He had never outgrown the infatuation that he felt for her.

anchors.claim: Vincent's secret panels contain hidden papers and ruby
